dedupe_keys.name: yemen civilian impact monitoring project data on incidents affecting civilian structures and infrastructure

description: The Civilian Impact Monitoring Project was a monitoring mechanism for real-time collection, analysis and dissemination of open source data on the civilian impact of armed violence in Yemen, run as a service under the United Nations Protection Cluster for Yemen and live from 1 August 2018, reporting nationally across five hubs: Al-Hudaydah, Sa'ada, Sana'a, Aden and Ibb. This dataset counts incidents that affected civilian houses, farms, vehicles, businesses and markets, and incidents that affected civilian infrastructure sites, since December 2017. It is published on the Humanitarian Data Exchange as two downloadable CSV files under CC BY, with a dataset date of 30 April 2021, and the methodology is described on the project website. Caveats: the organisation is marked inactive, the data are incident counts from open sources, not asset-level damage assessments, and coverage ends in 2021. It is useful for conflict-related hazard exposure and security threat analysis of civilian infrastructure, for calibrating attack frequencies in resilience scenarios and for emergency response planning in conflict settings; a related record is the IDMC displacement database.
